// comments: GEDCOM has no comment syntax. The key is omitted rather than declared empty so VS Code disables the toggle-comment commands instead of inserting nothing.
// wordPattern: Two alternatives. The first selects a whole cross-reference including its at-signs, so double-clicking @I1@ selects the identifier rather than a fragment. The second is a run of anything that is not whitespace, an at-sign or a solidus: deliberately not [A-Za-z] so that double-clicking a name works in every script, and stopping at the solidus so a surname selects on its own inside NAME John /Smith/.
// autoClosingPairs: Typing @ closes the pair, because a pointer is the most common reason to type one. The previous configuration excluded string scopes, which disabled it inside payloads — exactly where pointers are written. autoCloseBefore keeps it out of the way mid-word, so an email address in a note does not fight the editor.
// surroundingPairs: Selecting a surname and pressing / wraps it, which is how GEDCOM marks the surname component of a personal name.
// onEnterRules: GEDCOM has no indentation to continue, but it does have one unambiguous case: on a CONT line the next line is almost always another CONT at the same level. onEnterRules can only append static text, so each level is spelled out. Levels beyond 5 are rare enough not to be worth the noise.
// indentationRules: Deliberately absent. GEDCOM nests by level number with every line at column zero, so indentation-based rules have nothing to act on. Folding is provided by the language server instead.
